item.title: Beaches
item.description:
Honestly, you can’t go wrong with beaches on Lanta — the west coast has many beaches. What follows is a guide to how they differ so you can pick the right one for the day.

Khlong Dao Beach #

Khlong Dao Beach - The northernmost of the main beaches, closest to Saladan. A long, wide stretch of gently shelving sand that’s great for swimming and families, with plenty of restaurants, bars and resorts along the back. Recommended bar: Majestic bar

Long Beach (Phra Ae) #

Long Beach - Just south of Khlong Dao and, as the name suggests, very long. A popular base with lots of accommodation, beach bars and sunset spots, but still spacious enough to find a quiet stretch. Lym’s Bar is where most nomads go for sunset drinks.

Nui Bay #

Nui Bay - A small, beautiful cove reached by some steep steps. There are no real facilities here — sometimes there are monkeys, and sometimes someone selling drinks, but that’s about it. Come for the scenery and seclusion rather than amenities, keep an eye on your belongings around the monkeys, and bring what you need with you.

Beautiful Beach & Secret Beach #

Beautiful Beach - A gorgeous cove further south. Since 2026 there is a parking fee, and a gate that is closed at night, so plan around that if you’re heading out for sunset.

Secret Beach - Tucked in right next to Beautiful Beach. To reach it you park at Beautiful Beach and walk over — there’s no separate access — so the same parking fee and night gate apply. No facilities and no bars.

item.title: Coworking spaces
item.description:
Koh Lanta has four coworking spaces (KoHub, Monkey Business, Fika and Coworx) and several cafes that work just as well for a day at the laptop. The island has fiber internet along the west coast from Saladan down to Klong Nin. Cafes average around 180 Mbps, and the dedicated coworking spaces hit 1 Gbps. You won’t have connectivity problems here.

Coworking spaces #

KoHub #

KoHub is the biggest coworking space on the island. It’s off the main road near Long Beach, about 10 minutes walk from the sand, with a jungle garden out back. The internet is fast (1 Gbps fiber), there’s good coffee and food on site, and the community is the main draw. People come back year after year.

item.description:
Medical #

You can walk in to all clinics. Dr. Salarin is a good GP on Long Beach. For something more advanced with testing, Dr. Pad in Saladan is a good option. Dr. Pad also offers the Qdenga dengue vaccine (two doses, three months apart). Thonburi Lanta offers 24-hour emergency care.

Dentists #

  • Lanta Dente - Only dentist on the island, on Khlong Dao road.

item.title: Visa and immigration
item.description:
Most visitors get 30 days visa-free in Thailand, and you can extend that once by another 30 days. There’s no immigration office on Koh Lanta itself, so extensions mean a trip to Krabi Town. Visa agents on the island can help with the paperwork.

⚠️ Changed on 15 September 2026: Thailand cut visa-free stays from 60 to 30 days and shortened the list of eligible countries to 60 countries and territories (official notice in the Royal Gazette, in Thai; English list). A lot of websites still say 60 days. Check that your country is on the list before you book.

item.title: Getting to Koh Lanta
item.description:
Most people get to Koh Lanta by flying to Krabi and taking a road transfer of about 2 hours. Koh Lanta has no airport, and there’s no road bridge from the mainland yet, so every route ends with either a car ferry or a boat.

Check the visa rules for Koh Lanta before you book: since September 2026 most nationalities get 30 days visa-free, not 60.

Pick your route #

From Best route Door to door
Krabi Airport Shared minivan or private transfer 2-2.5 hrs + ferry queue
Bangkok Fly to Krabi, then transfer 5-6 hrs
Chiang Mai Direct flight to Krabi, then transfer 6-7 hrs
Phuket, Phi Phi, Ao Nang Ferry or speedboat (see below) 45 min-4 hrs

By ferry from other islands #

During high season (November to April), ferries connect Koh Lanta to Phuket, Phi Phi, Ao Nang, and other islands. Many routes run a reduced service or stop in low season.

item.title: Trips & Activities
item.description:
Cooking Classes #

Time for Lime #

The original Thai cooking school on Koh Lanta, open since 2002. Located on Klong Dao Beach in an open-air beachfront setting with a pool. Classes run ~5.5 hours — you make curry paste, 2 starters, and 2 main courses, then eat what you cooked. A cocktail class is included in some packages. Recipes are sent home with you.

A portion of all profits goes to Lanta Animal Welfare, which rescues and treats stray animals on the island.

item.title: Accommodation
item.description:
Most nomads stay around Long Beach (Phra Ae) since it’s close to KoHub. Prices vary a lot by season. High season (Dec-Feb) books up fast and costs roughly double what you’d pay in shoulder months (Nov, Mar-Apr). If you’re coming in peak season, book ahead. Outside of that, you can often just show up and walk around.

Some places are cheaper when you message them directly on WhatsApp or Facebook. Monthly rates are almost always negotiable in person.

item.title: Gyms and fitness
item.description:
Koh Lanta has two air-conditioned gyms, WM Fitness in the Long Beach area and Luke’s Gym in Klong Khong. Both charge 200 THB for a day pass. There’s also a cheap beach gym where your entry fee gets you a food and drink voucher, plus a few group fitness classes.

Gyms #

WM Fitness #

WM Fitness - Long Beach area. Modern gym with good selection of cardio equipment, resistance machines, and free weights. Also has a rig area with battle ropes, sandbags, kettlebells. Connected to William Muay Thai Stadium. Air conditioned. Day pass 200 THB. See Facebook for full pricing information.

item.title: Parties
item.description:
There is a more or less fixed schedule for the parties on the island. The big ones have a fixed day of the week. Some bars are a bit hidden but when they are the main party that night there will be torches outside on the main road to guide you there.

Pub Quiz at the Irish Embassy - The island’s proper Irish pub in Long Beach, going since 2006. Guinness, live sport on the screens, pool, darts and pub food. It is on the main road, so not a beach party.

item.title: Phone, laptop and scooter repair
item.description:
Need a phone, laptop or scooter repaired on Koh Lanta? These are the places nomads and locals use. Things break fast in the heat and humidity.

Laptops #

We don’t currently have a laptop repair place we can vouch for — the previous one (Ek) is permanently closed. If you know a good one, please let us know.

  • TAB Computer does computer repairs, but we haven’t been there yet.

Phones #

  • lantamobiles (ANJ)
  • 116 ID Mobile

Scooters #

Flat tires and other scooter issues: Phut Yanyon (พุฒยานยนต์) in Sala Dan.

item.title: Is there Grab on Koh Lanta?
item.description:
No. Grab doesn’t work on Koh Lanta, and neither does Bolt or any other ride-hailing app. The island is too small and too far from the mainland for any of them to operate here.

If you’re coming from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, or even Krabi town, you’re used to opening an app and having a car show up. That won’t happen here.

Need a ride right now? Message one of the taxi drivers below. Flying into Krabi? Book an airport transfer ahead of time.

item.title: Transportation
item.description:
There’s no public transport on Koh Lanta. Most people rent a scooter and that’s pretty much all you need. The island is about 30km from north to south, so even the longest trip only takes around 40 minutes.

Getting to the island #

Most people fly into Krabi and take a shared minivan or private transfer to Koh Lanta, about 2 to 2.5 hours including the car ferry. See Krabi Airport to Koh Lanta for prices and transfer companies, or getting to Koh Lanta for all routes.

item.title: ATMs and money exchange
item.description:
Cash is king on Koh Lanta, so you’ll be using ATMs and money exchange booths a lot. Most local restaurants, massage shops, markets and small businesses only accept cash. Bigger restaurants, hotels and convenience stores like 7-Eleven take Visa and Mastercard, but don’t count on it everywhere. Always have cash on hand.

Photo by Q L on Pexels (free to use)

ATMs #

ATMs are scattered across the island, mostly at 7-Elevens and bank branches. You’ll find them in Saladan, Klong Dao, Long Beach and Klong Nin. There are two banks in Saladan (SCB and TTB), and a Kasikorn ATM near Southern Lanta Resort at Klong Dao Beach.

item.title: Bangkok to Koh Lanta
item.description:
The fastest way from Bangkok to Koh Lanta is a flight to Krabi and a transfer to the island. Count on 5-6 hours door to door with a shared minivan, or 4-5 hours with a private car. There’s no airport on Koh Lanta.

Fly to Krabi (the easy option) #

Flights take about 1.5 hours and there are dozens a day from both Bangkok airports:

  • Suvarnabhumi (BKK): Bangkok Airways, Thai AirAsia, Thai Airways and Thai Vietjet
  • Don Mueang (DMK): Thai AirAsia, Nok Air and Thai Lion Air

Booked a few weeks ahead, one-way fares are often around 900-2,000 THB. From Krabi Airport it’s about 2 hours by car to the island, plus the car ferry. See Krabi Airport to Koh Lanta for minivans, private transfers and what to do if you land late.

item.title: Chiang Mai to Koh Lanta
item.description:
The quickest way from Chiang Mai to Koh Lanta is a direct flight to Krabi, then a transfer to the island. The flight takes about 2 hours and the transfer 2 to 2.5 hours, so count on 6-7 hours door to door.

Direct flights to Krabi #

  • Thai AirAsia flies Chiang Mai to Krabi direct two to three times a day. The morning flight gets you to Koh Lanta by early afternoon.
  • Bangkok Airways flies direct a few times a week, in the winter season only.

Other airlines (Thai Lion Air, Nok Air, Thai Airways, Thai Vietjet) connect through Bangkok, even when booking sites call the flight “direct”. With a connection, count on 7-9 hours or more door to door.

item.title: Krabi Airport to Koh Lanta
item.description:
Krabi Airport is the closest airport to Koh Lanta, about 75 km away. A private car takes around 2 hours and a shared minivan 2 to 2.5 hours, plus whatever time you spend waiting for the car ferry. Koh Lanta has no airport of its own.

Shared minivan #

The cheapest way to the island. Expect to pay about 400-550 THB per person, with drop-off at your hotel. You can buy a ticket at the transport counters in the arrivals hall or book online in advance (12Go and similar sites), which is usually a bit cheaper than buying at the counter.
